channel.title: Creatures on Core Keeper Hub
channel.description: Recent content in Creatures on Core Keeper Hub

item.title: Big Larva
item.description: The Big Larva is an aggressive hostile worm of The Clay Caves and the Larva Hive. It is a larger cousin of the common Larva and will chew through your base if left unchecked. Where to find it It spawns in The Clay Caves and the Larva Hive Biome, respawning on Chrysalis tiles. Combat tips Larva aggro on torches first — they prefer lit player objects over other targets, and will attack many player-placed base buildings Melee deals 93 damage with 412 HP; keep your distance and kite Immune to slow from slime and immune to acid damage Because it targets torches, it can be lured away from your camp Drops Larva Meat — 82.

item.title: Blackbug
item.description: Blackbug is a critter in Core Keeper. Unlike hostile mobs, critters are peaceful creatures you can catch with a Bug Net and keep or feed. Where to find it It frequently spawns when destroying wooden objects — breaking Wood, Coral Wood or Gleam Wood has a 15% chance to spawn one, while breaking wooden crates (such as Wooden Crates and Large Crates) has a 30% chance to spawn 1–2 (or 5–8 from large crates).

item.title: Blue Slime
item.description: Blue Slime is a hostile enemy mob in Core Keeper found in The Sunken Sea. It hops at you like other slimes, but its hits apply a slippery movement debuff that knocks both players and opposing mobs skidding across the ground. Where to find it It spawns naturally in The Sunken Sea, respawning periodically on Ground Slippery Slime tiles. Combat tips Stay off the slippery tiles when fighting: with 1,350 HP and 194 jump damage, it is far tougher than early slimes — don’t get knocked around on its home turf Slippery on hit: it knocks you back and applies slippery movement, which can slide you into other Sunken Sea hazards Immunities: immune to slime slow and slippery movement itself Drops Slippery Slime (94.

item.title: Bomb Scarab
item.description: The Bomb Scarab is a flying hostile scarab of The Desert of Beginnings. It dives through players, then — once hurt badly enough — channels and detonates, breaking nearby walls and objects. Where to find it It spawns in The Desert of Beginnings, rarely respawning on Desert Sand Ground inside the desert biome. Scarab ambushes also burrow out of the ground in groups, and Ra-Akar the Sand Titan summons them as adds during the boss fight.

item.title: Caveling
item.description: The Caveling is the basic hostile mob of The Undergrounds, found near the starting area. Low health and telegraphed attacks make it an easy first combat target. Tips Attacks are telegraphed — dodge sideways, not backwards Drops Caveling Remains used in early crafting

item.title: Caveling Assassin
item.description: The Caveling Assassin is a fast Desert caveling that fires a spread of three daggers and then dashes straight through its target. Its high speed and pass-through movement make it hard to pin down. Tips Data sourced from the Core Keeper wiki (atma.gg); numbers shift with patches Bring appropriate resistance gear before farming this area

item.title: Caveling Brute
item.description: The Caveling Brute is a slow but hard-hitting melee enemy found in The Undergrounds and The Clay Caves. It hits much harder than a normal Caveling — don’t tank its swings. Combat tips Dodge, don’t block: its swings are telegraphed; sidestep rather than trading hits Kite it: it’s slower than the player, so attack between its swing cooldowns Iron gear comfort: with 140 HP and 16 damage, it’s manageable in copper but much safer in tin+ Drops Caveling Remains (common) — salvage/repair material Iron Ore (common) — early source before you reach The Forgotten Ruins

item.title: Caveling Gardener
item.description: The Caveling Gardener patrols Azeos’ Wilderness on Lush Moss, circling players before striking. While standing on grass it can sprout up to five Snare Plants that trap you in place. Tips Data sourced from the Core Keeper wiki (atma.gg); numbers shift with patches Bring appropriate resistance gear before farming this area

item.title: Caveling Hunter
item.description: Caveling Hunter is a hostile enemy mob in Core Keeper. These sneaky snipers temporarily disguise themselves as a Wilderness Bush, then snipe players with a Flintlock Musket from surprisingly long range — sometimes almost off-screen. Where to find it It spawns naturally in Azeos’ Wilderness, respawning periodically on Lush Moss tiles. Combat tips Watch the bushes: it pretends to be a bush until you get close — scan suspicious foliage before walking past Close the distance: it wants to keep range; the musket projectile is fast but the rate of fire is slow, so dash between shots Ranged answers work too: return fire from beyond its preferred musket band while it keeps kiting 870 HP, 152 range damage: don’t let it chip you from off-screen while you fight other mobs Drops Lush Moss (2.

item.title: Caveling Mummy
item.description: Caveling Mummy is a hostile enemy mob in Core Keeper. A mold-infected undead caveling wandering The Desert of Beginnings, it is best known for dropping the Zealot’s Scimitar, the Puppet Ring and the pajama clothing set. Where to find it It spawns in The Desert of Beginnings (mold-infected faction). Combat tips High health pool: 1,836 HP — expect longer fights than ordinary desert mobs Damage value: not listed on the wiki page (data待核) — treat it as a mid-tier desert threat and don’t face-tank unarmored Farm it for gear: its interesting drops (Zealot’s Scimitar, Puppet Ring, pajama set) sit around a ~2.

item.title: Caveling Scholar
item.description: The Caveling Scholar appears in Forlorn Metropolis dungeons, firing a Scholar’s Staff at range and beaming heals onto nearby Scholars and Core Sentries. Take them out first or the whole room will sustain itself. Tips Data sourced from the Core Keeper wiki (atma.gg); numbers shift with patches Bring appropriate resistance gear before farming this area

item.title: Caveling Skirmisher
item.description: The Caveling Skirmisher is a ranged mob of The Clay Caves that hurls spears on sight from Clay Moss tiles. Weaker than melee cavelings but annoying at range, it drops Larva Meat and Fiber when farmed. Tips Data sourced from the Core Keeper wiki (atma.gg); numbers shift with patches Bring appropriate resistance gear before farming this area

item.title: Caveling Spearman
item.description: Caveling Spearman is a hostile enemy mob in Core Keeper found in The Clay Caves. It is the close-quarters melee counterpart to the spear-throwing Caveling Skirmisher — a low-health early cave mob you will meet constantly while mining clay. Where to find it It spawns naturally in The Clay Caves, respawning on Clay Moss tiles. Combat tips Treat it as basic fodder: only 270 HP and a 74-damage melee hit — safe in copper gear once you understand its swing Don’t stand in clusters: Clay Moss spawns it alongside Skirmishers that throw spears from range; kite the group rather than face-tanking Cheap farm target: reliable early Larva Meat and Fiber source while exploring the caves Drops Fiber (22.

item.title: Citrus Pinion
item.description: Citrus Pinion is a flying critter in Core Keeper. Unlike hostile mobs, critters are peaceful creatures you can catch with a Bug Net and keep or feed. It flutters erratically with bright colors that are irritating to the naked eye. Where to find it It spawns naturally in Azeos’ Wilderness. How to catch Equip a Bug Net and swing at it as you walk close Critters can be placed back in the world as persistent decoration Sell value: 1 Feeding Can be fed to Strolly Poly or Dodo.

item.title: Clay Burrower
item.description: The Clay Burrower is an aggressive burrowing enemy found in The Clay Caves. It is a larva-faction mob with a rounded, earthen body. Where to find it It spawns in The Clay Caves. Combat tips It is an aggressive (hostile) mob with 405 HP Attack numbers are not listed on the wiki page — treat its melee hits as mid-range Clay Caves damage and dodge normally The wiki rolls 1–2 drops per kill, so loot per fight can vary Drops Marbled Meat — 28.

item.title: Colossal Amoeba
item.description: The Colossal Amoeba is a huge hostile blob that drifts through The Passage. With 5,535 HP it is one of the tankiest mobs of the Passage region. Where to find it It spawns naturally in The Passage. Combat tips Extremely high health (5,535 HP) — commit before engaging; bring crowd control Wiki page is currently a stub: attack damage not yet documented (数据待核) Reliable source of Cytoplasm and the crafting item Sulfur Bomb Drops Cytoplasm — 85.

item.title: Core Sentry
item.description: The Core Sentry is a large Forlorn Metropolis construct that stays dormant until you approach, then powers up and stomps a three-way fork of bright projectiles. Very high health makes it a priority target. Tips Data sourced from the Core Keeper wiki (atma.gg); numbers shift with patches Bring appropriate resistance gear before farming this area

item.title: Dusk Fairy

It is a tiny butterfly with very delicate wings; catching it without harming them requires a lot of caution. Where to find it It spawns naturally in Azeos’ Wilderness. How to catch Equip a Bug Net and swing at it as you walk close — approach gently, as its delicate wings are easily harmed Critters can be placed back in the world as persistent decoration Sell value: 1 Feeding Can be fed to Strolly Poly or Dodo.

Where to find it It spawns naturally in The Undergrounds, The Clay Caves, and Azeos’ Wilderness. A worm — nothing special about it. How to catch Equip a Bug Net and swing at it as you walk close Critters can be placed back in the world as persistent decoration Sell value: 1 Feeding Can be fed to Strolly Poly or Dodo.

item.title: Electro-Pest
item.description: The Electro-Pest is a rare hostile pest found in The Forgotten Ruins. It belongs to the Abiotic Factor Facility scene — don’t confuse it with the friendly pet Electro-Pet. Where to find it It spawns inside the Abiotic Factor Facility scene in The Forgotten Ruins. Only 8 Electro-Pests exist per world and they never respawn, so treat each encounter as limited. Combat tips Limited per world — do not waste the encounter; it will not come back Wiki page is currently a stub: attack damage not yet documented (数据待核) It drops event-themed gear such as the Quill Rifle and Bottled Anomaly Drops Scrap Parts — 57.

item.title: Gem Snail
item.description: Gem Snail is a critter in Core Keeper. Unlike hostile mobs, critters are peaceful creatures you can catch with a Bug Net and keep or feed. Where to find it It slowly crawls through the dangers of The Shimmering Frontier — a small snail carrying a gleaming gem-like shell. How to catch Equip a Bug Net and swing at it as you walk close Critters can be placed back in the world as persistent decoration Sell value: 1 Loot when caught: Crystal Snail (~10% per roll, 1–2 rolls); Large Sun Crystal (~7.

item.title: Ice Wind
item.description: Ice Wind is a flying critter in Core Keeper. Unlike hostile mobs, critters are peaceful creatures you can catch with a Bug Net and keep or feed. This blue butterfly flaps its wings so fast that it creates cold air streams. Where to find it It spawns naturally in The Sunken Sea. How to catch Equip a Bug Net and swing at it as you walk close Critters can be placed back in the world as persistent decoration Sell value: 1 Feeding Can be fed to Strolly Poly or Dodo.

item.title: Infected Caveling
item.description: Infected Caveling is a hostile enemy mob in Core Keeper. A mold-corrupted caveling that walks very slowly like a zombie, then lunges a short distance to melee. Its hits can poison you — a debuff that greatly reduces healing received. Where to find it It spawns naturally in the Mold Biome sub-areas of Azeos’ Wilderness, respawning periodically on Mold Ground tiles. Combat tips Slow but damaging: it lumbers toward you, then lunges — 194 melee damage is no joke; keep your distance and kite Mind the poison: hits have a chance to apply poison, cutting healing received by 75% — don’t rely on potions to save you mid-fight It’s immune to mold infection, so mold-based tricks won’t work on it Drops Scrap Parts (8.

item.title: Larvlet
item.description: Larvlet is a critter in Core Keeper. Unlike hostile mobs, critters are peaceful creatures you can catch with a Bug Net and keep or feed. Where to find it It spawns naturally in The Clay Caves. Destroying a Cocoon also has a 50% chance to spawn between 2 and 5 Larvlets. It is a tiny larva that doesn’t harm you but likes to be collected and held in a warm hand.

item.title: Mold Tentacle
item.description: The Mold Tentacle is a hostile mold mob found in the Mold Biome of Azeos’ Wilderness. It glows faintly in the dark, so you can spot it long before it spots you — and it lob projectiles that leave players stunned. Where to find it It spawns in the Mold Biome (a sub-biome of Azeos’ Wilderness), respawning on Mold Ground. Combat tips Its ranged attack deals 173 damage and hard-stuns for 1–2 seconds on hit Several tentacles together can stun-lock you, buying time for Infected Cavelings to close to melee range — kill tentacles first Immune to mold infection Faint glow gives away its position in the dark; engage from range Drops Ancient Coin — 13.

item.title: Moon Pincher
item.description: Moon Pincher is a critter in Core Keeper. Unlike hostile mobs, critters are peaceful creatures you can catch with a Bug Net and keep or feed. Where to find it It spawns naturally in The Sunken Sea. This blue-purple crustacean always has its claws raised, which gives it a seemingly happy expression. How to catch Equip a Bug Net and swing at it as you walk close Critters can be placed back in the world as persistent decoration Sell value: 1 Feeding Can be fed to Strolly Poly, Dodo or Orex — a handy way to feed farm animals without spending crops.

item.title: Nilipede
item.description: The Nilipede is a hostile crystal creature that prowls The Shimmering Frontier. A long, gem-encrusted centipede with a lot of HP, it is one of the late-frontier mobs you will run into alongside Mimites. Where to find it It spawns naturally in The Shimmering Frontier. Combat tips High health pool (2,670 HP) — bring your best frontier-tier weapon Wiki page is currently a stub: attack damage not yet documented (数据待核) Farming it is the source of the Ninja armor set and the Ricochet Shuriken Drops Marbled Meat — 26.

item.title: Orange Slime
item.description: Orange Slime (also called a slime blob, or just “slime”) is a neutral enemy mob in Core Keeper. It is passive until attacked — one of the least dangerous enemies in the game thanks to its low damage and passivity. Where to find it It spawns on Ground Slime tiles in The Undergrounds and The Clay Caves. Combat tips Leave it alone: it won’t attack until hit, so you can walk past safely When provoked: it hops on you for 31 jump damage — trivial, but it will also aggro onto your Spike Traps, making them free slime cleaners Immunities: immune to slime slow and acid damage Drops Slime (58.

item.title: Orex
item.description: Orex is a cattle (farm animal) in Core Keeper. Unlike small critters, it is not caught with a Bug Net — it is raised as livestock and fed. Where to find it Found in the Moss Sub Biome in The Forgotten Ruins. This cavernous carnivore has a surprisingly timid temper for having such sharp horns; its large serrated muzzle is sooner to swallow critters whole than to bite the hand that may feed it.

item.title: Pest Bug
item.description: Pest Bug is a critter in Core Keeper. Unlike hostile mobs, critters are peaceful creatures you can catch with a Bug Net and keep or feed. Where to find it It spawns naturally in The Forgotten Ruins. It is a disgusting insect that moves with uncanny speed, commonly found where there is darkness, dirt and food to offer. How to catch Equip a Bug Net and swing at it as you walk close Critters can be placed back in the world as persistent decoration Sell value: 1 Feeding Can be fed to Strolly Poly, Dodo or Orex — a handy way to feed farm animals without spending crops.

item.title: Purple Slime
item.description: The Purple Slime is the poison slime of Azeos’ Wilderness, spawning on Ground Poison Slime. Its jumps apply poison that cuts healing received by 75%, so keep antidotes or a Remedaisy Necklace ready. Tips Data sourced from the Core Keeper wiki (atma.gg); numbers shift with patches Bring appropriate resistance gear before farming this area

item.title: Red Slime
item.description: The Red Slime is the always-aggressive early slime of The Undergrounds and The Clay Caves. Unlike the passive Orange Slime it shares Ground Slime with, it will hop onto you on sight and is immune to slow and acid. Tips Data sourced from the Core Keeper wiki (atma.gg); numbers shift with patches Bring appropriate resistance gear before farming this area

Where to find it A dark little fellow with seemingly unseeing eyes that nevertheless seem to stare deep into your soul. Its exact spawn biome is Data pending verification（数据待核） — the official wiki page does not currently list its spawn location. How to catch Equip a Bug Net and swing at it as you walk close Critters can be placed back in the world as persistent decoration Sell value: 1 Feeding Can be fed to Strolly Poly, Dodo or Orex — a handy way to feed farm animals without spending crops.

item.title: Shrooman
item.description: The Shrooman is a weak mushroom enemy found in The Undergrounds. It has little health and slowly charges at anyone who wanders onto its fungal ground. Where to find it It respawns periodically on Fungal Soil in The Undergrounds. Larger Shrooman Brutes patrol the same ground. Combat tips Easy pickings — only 105 HP and a 39-damage dash ram Let it charge, sidestep, and hit after it whiffs Farm it for early Mushroom and seed drops Drops Mushroom (45.

item.title: Shrooman Brute
item.description: The Shrooman Brute is a large, aggressive mushroom enemy of The Undergrounds. It lumbers toward you, then charges — and its hard shell makes it surprisingly tanky. Where to find it It spawns in The Undergrounds, respawning periodically on Fungal Soil. Combat tips It charges slowly at opponents, dealing damage and knockback on impact Its shell reduces incoming damage to 1 while intact — be patient and chip it down If it rams a wall, chasm, or object while charging, it destroys those blocks and becomes stunned and vulnerable — bait charges into terrain It will not charge across a chasm — gaps are a safe barrier Charge attack damage is not listed on the wiki page (marked 数据待核) Drops Mushroom — 53.

item.title: Sniffling
item.description: Sniffling is a peaceful critter in Core Keeper, added with The Void & Voltage update. Unlike hostile mobs, critters are peaceful creatures you can catch with a Bug Net and keep or feed. It is a skittish little rodent that scurries around for hardened crumbs left in debris. Where to find it Data pending verification（数据待核）— the atma.gg page confirms it was added with The Void & Voltage update but does not yet list a specific spawn biome.

How to catch Equip a Bug Net and swing at it as you walk close Critters can be placed back in the world as persistent decoration Sell value: 1 Feeding Can be fed to Strolly Poly, Dodo or Orex — a handy way to feed farm animals without spending crops.

item.title: Sulfur Worm
item.description: The Sulfur Worm is a hostile worm that burrows through The Passage. It is one of the signature late-area mobs of the Passage, alongside the Colossal Amoeba. Where to find it It spawns naturally in The Passage. Combat tips Tanky (3,075 HP) — expect a longer fight than earlier biomes Wiki page is currently a stub: attack damage not yet documented (数据待核) Its drops are the basic Passage crafting materials Cytoplasm and Sulfur Bud Drops Cytoplasm — 49.

item.title: Tentacle
item.description: The Tentacle is a hostile sea creature found only in The Sunken Sea. It lobs small white jellyfish projectiles at range, hitting for 194 damage. Where to find it It spawns on water tiles in the Sea biome, most often on water adjacent to ground tiles (not bridges). It is rare in open water. Combat tips Close the distance — its jellyfish projectile is painful at range, so swim/bridge toward it With 945 HP it takes a few hits; use mid-tier sea gear (Octarine+) for comfort Fight from shore or on bridges to avoid being surrounded by other sea mobs Drops Octarine Ore (13.

item.title: Void Larvlet

Unlike hostile mobs, critters are peaceful creatures you can catch with a Bug Net and keep or feed. It is a tiny void larva that doesn’t harm you but likes to be collected and held in a warm hand. Where to find it Data pending verification（数据待核）— the atma.gg page confirms it was added with The Void & Voltage update but does not yet list a specific spawn biome.

item.title: Yellow Glowbug
item.description: The Yellow Glowbug is a flying critter in Core Keeper. Unlike hostile mobs, critters are peaceful creatures you can catch with a Bug Net. This one drifts in swarms that look like dancing lights and glows yellow. Where to find it It appears in swarms in The Undergrounds, The Clay Caves, and The Desert of Beginnings. Its yellow glow is specific to these biomes. How to catch Equip a Bug Net and swing at it as you walk close It is stationary once placed, and emits yellow light — a free, slot-free light source for your base Caught glowbugs can be placed back in the world as persistent decoration, but they still move around and die in a single hit if attacked Sell value: 1 Feeding Glowbugs are the one critter cattle will not eat — Strolly Poly, Dodo, and Orex eat all critters except glowbugs, so keep them as lighting rather than feed.
